THE PARLIAMENTARY DEBATES OFFICIAL REPORT IN THE HUNDRED 
AND NINETY FOURTH SESSION OF THE RAJYA SABHA 
Commencing on the 19th November. 2001/Kartika 28, 1923 (Saka) 

[19 November, 2001J RAJYA SABHA  
RAJYA SABHA Monday, the 19th 
November, 2001/28 Kartika, 1923 (Saka) 
The House met at eleven of the clock, 
MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair. 
The National Anthem "Jana Gana Mana" was played. 
OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the 
passing away of Shri K.P. Mailikarjunudu, Shri Shiv Pratap Mishra. Shri 
Surendranath Dwivedy, Shrimati Maragatham Chandrashekhar and Shri 
Shyamdhar Misra, former Members of this House. 
Shri Mailikarjunudu passed away on the 31B| August, 2001 at the age 
of 99, Born at Yelakurru Agraharam, Krishna District (Andhra Pradesh) in 
December, 1901, Shri Mailikarjunudu had his education at Machilipatnam and 
Madras. 
A lawyer by profession, Shri Mailikarjunudu was an active social and 
political worker. A veteran freedom fighter, he was imprisoned for six months 
and fined for taking part in individual Satyagraha. He actively took part in the 
Quit India Movement in 1942. Shri Mailikarjunudu had several publications to his 
credit. He was a Member of the then Madras Legislative C ouncil during 1937-
1940. Shri Mailikarjunudu represented t he State of Andhra Pradesh in this 
House from April, 1966 to April, 1972. 
In the passing away of Shri Mailikarjunudu, the country has lost a noted 
social worker and a veteran freedom fighter. 
Shri Shiv Pratap Mishra passed away on the 7 th September, 2001 at 
Allahabad. Born at .village Ramnagar, Distt. Pratapgarh (Uttar Pradesh), Shri 
Mishra had his education at Allahabad University. An advocate by profession, 
Shri Mishra joined the Bhoodan Movement and participated in the Padyatra, with 
Acharya Vinoba Bhave, in 1964. He was Chairman of the Programme 
Committee of the Indian Youth Congress and General-Secretary, Indian Youth 
Congress, in 1969. He was also leader of the Indian Youth Delegation to 
Moscow and Berlin. 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [19 November. 2001]  
Shri Mishra represented the State of Uttar Pradesh in this House 
from April, 1988 to April 1994.   During his membership in the House, he took 
keen interest in the proceedings of the House. 
In the passing away of Shri Mishra, the country has lost an active 
social worker and a noted Parliamentarian. 
Shri Surendra Nath Dwivedy passed away on the 1 8' October, 2001 
at Rourkela, at the age of 87. Born at  village Khandasahi, District Cuttak, in 
February, 1913, Shri Dwivedy plunged into the freedom struggle in his school 
days at an early age. He boycotted t he school during the Civil Disobedience 
Movement in 1930. He was imprisoned on several occasions and spent more 
than seven years in jail for the struggle against British imperialism. 
A journalist by profession, Shri Dwivedy was a whole-time political 
worker. He was associated with various kissan, yduth and other movements in 
Orissa. Shri Dwivedy was the founder-editor of "Krushak", an Oriya weekly. 
Shri Dwivedy represented the State of Orissa in this House from 
April. 1952 to April. 1956. He was also a Member of the 2 nd, 3rt and 4 m Lok 
Sabhas. During his Membership in the Lok Sabha, Shri Dwivedy served as a 
member of the Panel of Charimen, and Chairman of the Committee on Public 
Undertakings. Shri Dwivedy also served as Governor of Arunachal Pradesh 
from 1991 to 1993. 
In the passing away of Shri Dwivedy, the country has lost a veteran 
freedom fighter, a distinguished parliamentarian and a noted social worker. 
Shrimati Maragatham Chandrashekhar passed away on 26th October, 
2001. at the age of 83.   Bom at Madras in November, 1917, Smt. 
Chandrashekhar had her education at Madras and London, A teacher by 
vocation, Shrimati Chandrashekhar was an active political and social worker. 
She devoted her life to the upliftment of women, children, the Scheduled 
Castes and the Scheduled Tribes. She was also associated with the nationalist 
movement and took an active part in th e freedom struggle. She held the post 
of General-Secretary of the All-India Congress Committee in 1972. 
2 

[19 November, 2001] RAJYA SABHA  
Shrimati Chandrashekhar had a very long and distinguished 
parliamentary career. She was a Member of the First, Third, Fifth, Ninth and 
Tenth Lok Sabhas. She was also nominated to the Rajya Sabha for three 
consecutive terms - from April. 1970 to April, 1976; April, 1976 to April 1982; 
and, again, from September , 1982; and remained a Member of this House till 
December, 1984, when she got elected to the Lok Sabha. She also served as 
Union Minister for several years and held the portfolios of Health, Home 
Affairs, and Women and Social Welfare. 
A widely-travelled personality, Shrimati Chandrashekhar was a 
leader and member of various Indi an Parliamentary Delegations and 
represented India in several internatio nal events. She was also Chairman of 
the Commission for Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes, the National Small 
Industries Corporation, and the Commission for Linguistic Minorities of India. 
In the passing away of Shrimati Chandrashekhar, the country has 
lost an eminent social worker, a champion of the cause of upliftment of 
women and a veteran parliamentarian. 
Shri Shyamdhar Misra passed away on 4* November, 2001 at the 
age of 88. Born in July, 1918 at vill age Kathauta, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, 
Shri Misra had his education at the Banaras Hindu University and Allahabad 
University. 
A trader and agriculturist by profession, Shri Misra took an active part in 
the drive against untouchabiiity and propagation of widow marriage. He 
pioneered the co-operative movement in Banaras. He was Chairman of the 
Study Team for Pilot Project Industries, Co-operative Training Committee; 
Study Team for relationship of Panchayats to Co-operatives. He was also 
President, Super Bazar, the Cooperative Stores Ltd., New Delhi. 
The long and distinguished legislative career of Shri Misra started 
with membership of the erstwhile Banaras State Assembly from 1943 to 1949. 
Thereafter, he was a Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council from 
1950 to 1952. Shri Misra represented t he State of Uttar Pradesh in this House 
for three terms - from April, 1952 to April, 1958; April, 1958 to April, 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [19 November, 2001]  
1962; and, again, from April, 1968 to April, 1974, He was also a Member of 
the Third Lok Sabha. Shri Misra also served as Union Deputy Minister from 
1962 to 1967, and held the portfolios of Community Development, Panchayati 
Raj and Co-operation, Irrigation and Powe r, Defence, Food and Agriculture, 
Community Development and Co-operation. 
In the passing away of Shri Misra, the country has lost a pioneer in 
the field of cooperative movement, an able administrator and an eminent 
Parliamentarian. 
Hon'ble Members, this House also wishes to place on record its deep 
and heartfelt sorrow on the tragic and untimely demise of Shri Madhavrao 
Sctndia, a sitting Member of the Lok Sabha, on 30* September, 2001, in a 
plane crash in Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh, at the age of 56. 
Born in March, 1945 at Mumbai, Shri Scindia had his education at 
Sctndia School, Gwalior, Winchester College, and New College, Oxford {UK). 
A political and social worker, Shri Scindia was associated with several 
educational, cultural, sports and wildli fe preservation organisations, and was 
President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India from 1990 to 1993. He 
also held the post of General-Secreta ry of the All-India Congress Committee 
Since 1996-97. 
Shri Scindia started his long, dist inguished, legislative career when 
he was first elected in 1971 to the Fifth Lok Sabha and remained Member of 
the Sixth, Seventh, Eighth, Ninth, Tent h, Eleventh, Twelfth and Thirteenth Lok 
Sabhas. He was Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee on Science and 
Technology in 1990-1991. He was also Deputy Leader of the Congress Party 
in the Lok Sabha since 1999. 
Shri Scindia served in the Union Council of Ministers, as Cabinet 
Minister for several years, and held the portfolios of Railways during 1984-89, 
Civil Aviation during 1991-93, and' Human Resource Development during 
1995-96. As Union Railway Minister,, he was instrumental in computerizing 
Railway reservation in the country. 
A widely«travelled person, Shri Madhavrao Scindia was leader and 
member of various Indian Parliamentar y Delegations and represented India in 
several international events. In 1995, he chaired the Ministerial meeting of E-9 
countries at Bali (Indonesia). 
4 

119 November, 2001] RAJYA SABHA  
During his three decades of political career, Shri Scindia carved a 
niche for himself in politics, governm ent, and cricket. An eloquent speaker in 
both English and Hindi, he had the dist inction of winning all the Lok Sabha 
elections he contested. He was a man of high principles, and people's interest 
was uppermost in his mind. From politics to cricket, Shri Scindia distinguished 
himself with the true sporting spirit. He understood the pulse of Indian politics 
very well, and, over the years, mainta ined his reputation as one of the' most 
suave and articulate politicians in the country. Shri Madhavrao Scindia 
understood the perspective of Indi an industry and the socio-economic 
dimension of liberalisation. 
In the death of Shri Scindia, the country has lost a young, dynamic, 
mass leader, an able administrator and an eminent Parliamentarian. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of  Shri K.P. Mallikarjunudu, Shri 
Shiv Pratap Mishra, Shri Surendra Nath Dwivedy, Shrimati Maragatham 
Chandrashekhar, Shri Shyamdhar Misra and Shri Madhavrao Scindia. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General wi ll convey to the members of 
the bereaved families our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy. 
REFERENCE TO THE VICTIMS OF TERRORIST ATTACKS IN 
THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, this House wishes to place on 
record its heartfelt sympathies for the victims of terrorism, in India and in other 
parts of the world. For us in India, terrorism has a special resonance because 
we have been a victim of terrorism for ov er a decade, and we know what it is 
like to lose a loved one in a wanton terrorist attack. That is why India lost no 
time in lending its voice to the worid community in condemning the recent 
terrorist attacks in the United States, in which many Indians were among the 
victims. Our hearts go out to the families of those victims who are still trying to 
come to terms with the tragedy. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [19 November, 2001]  
While each such attack is an assault on freedom and democracy. the 
attacks of September 11 in New York an d Washington, as, indeed, the attack 
of October 1, in Srinagar, brought .home to the world just how far and wide the 
tentacles of terrorism have spread, and what resources and organisational 
capability they have at their command to  hit targets, not onfy across borders 
but also across continents. 
Terrorism has, today, emerged as the biggest challenge facing the 
world. It is imperative for the world commu nity to stand together in the fight to 
destroy and defeat the global terror network, wherever it exists. 
I, now, request Members to rise in their places and observe silence 
as a mark of respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in this 
tragedy. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
REFERENCE TO BOMB BLAST AT JAMMU AND KASHMIR ASSEMBLY 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer, with profound sorrow, to the killing of 
39 persons and injury to 60 others, by a suicide squad of Jaish-e-Mohammad, a 
terrorist outfit, on the 1 s1 October. 2001, in an attempt to storm the J and K 
Assembly. I am sure, the whole House will join me in condemning this inhuman 
and dastardly act of hate and terror, which has shocked the entire world. In this 
hour of tragedy, we extend our heartfelt condolences to the affected families in 
their hour of grief and also pray for the early recovery of those who have been 
injured. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in this tragedy. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: As a mark of respect to the memory of Shri 
Madhavrao Scindia, a sitting Member of the Lok Sabha, the House   stands   
adjourned   till   11    A.M.   on   Tuesday,   the   20,h 
November, 2001. 
The House then adjourned at sixteen minutes past eleven of the clock, till 
eleven of the clock on Tuesday, the 20"1 November, 2001.
